methodological_rigor.justification: IBI334 bispecific antibody characterization is methodologically rigorous: cryo-EM structure resolved to 2.98 Angstrom with full structural validation, in vitro binding and effector function assays with appropriate controls, xenograft efficacy studies across multiple tumor lines, NHP GLP toxicology to 120 mg/kg with NOAEL determination, and phase 1 FIH trial safety data from NCT05774873. The cryo-EM resolution and structural analysis of B7-H3-mediated cis-inhibition are technically sound. Group sizes in animal studies are appropriate. The phase 1 safety data are preliminary (n not fully specified) and descriptive only.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical-to-early-clinical pipeline study for a novel B7-H3/EGFR bispecific antibody with cryo-EM structural characterization. The NHP GLP safety data and phase 1 FIH dose escalation initiation represent significant clinical translation steps. Clinical relevance is supported by B7-H3 and EGFR co-expression across multiple solid tumor types. However, phase 1 efficacy data are not yet available, keeping the study primarily at preclinical LoE 5 with early clinical safety signal.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE adherence is good for animal study components: model descriptions, group sizes, ethical approvals, and statistical methods are described. Cryo-EM data deposition in PDB is mentioned and represents best practice for structural biology. NHP toxicology study details (GLP certification, species, duration, dosing) are appropriately reported. Phase 1 trial is registered (NCT05774873). Raw cryo-EM data availability beyond PDB deposition is not specified; pharmacokinetic raw data are not shared.

novelty_literature.justification: The cryo-EM characterization revealing B7-H3-mediated cis-inhibition as a mechanism by which EGFR signaling is modulated upon IBI334 bispecific binding is a genuinely novel structural insight. The bispecific design targeting B7-H3 and EGFR simultaneously fills a documented gap in targeting heterogeneous tumors with mixed antigen expression. The structural basis for dual-targeting and the NHP safety data together represent a substantive preclinical-to-translational package.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript integrates structural biology, pharmacology, and clinical translation in a well-organized narrative. Cryo-EM structure figures and the binding interface diagrams are clear and publication quality. In vivo tumor growth curves and NHP safety tables are appropriately presented. The discussion contextualizes IBI334 within the B7-H3 and bispecific antibody therapeutic landscape. Minor: the phase 1 data section is brief and could more clearly distinguish preliminary safety observations from efficacy signals.

key_strengths: High-resolution cryo-EM structure at 2.98 Angstrom revealing novel B7-H3 cis-inhibition mechanism is a first-in-class structural finding
Comprehensive preclinical-to-clinical package: in vitro, xenograft, GLP NHP toxicology, and phase 1 initiation
NHP GLP toxicology to 120 mg/kg with established NOAEL provides robust safety foundation
B7-H3/EGFR bispecific design rationally addresses tumor antigen heterogeneity
key_concerns: Phase 1 efficacy data not yet available; clinical section is limited to safety signal only
Raw cryo-EM data and pharmacokinetic data deposition policies not fully specified
B7-H3 cis-inhibition mechanism described structurally but functional consequence on downstream signaling not fully characterized
Xenograft tumor models limited to immunodeficient mice, not capturing immune microenvironment interactions
chief_reviewer.rationale: A well-executed bispecific antibody development study with novel structural insights and a rigorous preclinical-to-early-clinical package; minor revisions to clarify data deposition and expand the mechanistic characterization of cis-inhibition will support Tier 2 publication in translational oncology journals.
